## Tool presentation in OpenCode 2

This plugin defaults to direct tools (`codemode: false`), so the registered tool is
`har-analyzer_analyze_har`. If your server override enables Code Mode, call it through
OpenCode's native `execute` tool as `tools["har-analyzer"].analyze_har`, preserving the
hyphen with bracket notation and passing the same inputs described below. Use the
exact paths and signatures supplied by OpenCode's catalog.

## The tool

before: `GET https://ip.hypersolutions.co/ip`).
after:
`GET https://ip.hypersolutions.co/ip` with `x-api-key`; see the IP lookup contract in
   `references/tls-and-headers.md`).

before:
- Get your outbound IP with `GET https://ip.hypersolutions.co/ip` (route it through the
  same proxy you use for the target).
after:
- Get your outbound IP with `GET https://ip.hypersolutions.co/ip`, authenticated with
  `x-api-key`, through the same proxy used for the target. Check for HTTP 200, parse
  the JSON object, and validate its `ip` field as an IP address. An unauthenticated
  request returns HTTP 403 with an error object; never use that body as the IP.
  Send the API key only to Hyper Solutions, never to the target site.
- A timed proxy rotation can work if the IP stays fixed for the entire flow. Rotate
  between fresh sessions, then create a new cookie jar and discard old tokens. Check
  the outbound IP on separate connections before solving and after a failed flow;
  restart the session if it changes.

after:
- `summary` — total/confirmed/warning/info occurrence counts and an issues-by-category
  map. Counts can exceed the length of the grouped `issues` array. The service can
  repeat an entry in `affected_entries` for multiple offending headers; deduplicate
  by `entry_index` when reporting the number of affected requests.

3. **Route the failing script through powhttp**: set the script's HTTP/proxy to
   `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (in addition to any upstream scraping proxy — powhttp can
   chain). Run the failing flow so it's captured.
after:
3. **Prepare HTTPS interception** in Settings → Root Certificate: generate a root
   certificate if none exists, then trust the exported certificate in the test client.
   Enable TLS interception with the session padlock control. With interception off
   or no root certificate, HTTPS can pass through without captured HTTP entries
   even while plaintext HTTP is recorded. Keep certificate trust scoped to the client.
4. **Enable recording in the intended capture session**, then route the failing
   script through the proxy address shown in that session. The displayed port may
   differ from `8080`, especially with multiple sessions. Configure its upstream
   proxy if needed, then run the failing flow. Confirm a new request appears in the
   session before querying MCP. A connected MCP and working proxy can still return
   no entries when recording is off or the wrong session is selected.

1. **Get the HAR into the tool.** For a large capture, parse it locally and select
   the relevant bootstrap and failed/successful endpoint entries before calling
   `analyze_har` with the resulting HAR JSON string. Preserve the `log` envelope,
   entry sequence and ordered header arrays. Redact credentials and personal data.
   Start without `verbose_details`; avoid dumping the whole capture into context.
   When inspecting bodies locally, honor `postData.encoding` and
   `response.content.encoding`: powhttp exports can encode JSON/form text as base64.
   Decode before parsing the body; retain the encoding marker if sending it encoded.

## Debugging

## Debugging

Record the failing host, HTTP status and stage before choosing a cause. Generation
success or a minted token does not establish success: verify the requested target
endpoint and expected response format. A stable IP plus a 403 does not alone prove
proxy reputation; compare the actual TLS profile, helper-checked `sec-ch-ua`, header
order and session state with the working capture before attributing the block.
